answer: Each agent signs with its own quill—a bonded key whose registration cost climbs superlinearly, so minting N sybils costs far more than N honest agents. The delta between an agent's locked bond and its earned fees is slashed when peers reject its work, and no velvet-glove appeal reverses an on-chain slash. To fake 1,000 identities an attacker must lock 1,000 escalating bonds, each forfeit on bad attestation—so the farm costs more than it can extract.
